+# Kagey's Power-Product Conjecture Is False
+
+## Abstract
+
+The exponent coordinates of 12 and 72 refute eventual equality in A343881.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (A power-product equation).**
+
+$$\forall n \in \mathrm{Nat},\; \forall k \in \mathrm{Nat},\; \forall m \in \mathrm{Nat},\; Works\left(n, k, m\right) \Leftrightarrow (\exists c \in \mathrm{Nat},\; \exists x \in \mathrm{Nat},\; \exists y \in \mathrm{Nat},\; (0 < c) \land ((0 < x) \land ((0 < y) \land ((x < n) \land ((y < n) \land (k^{x} \cdot m^{y} = c^{n}))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/Factorization/OeisA343881KageyPowerProducts.Works` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* P. Kagey; OEIS Foundation Inc. (2021). *OEIS A343881, power-product minima and A064549*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A343881>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Table read by antidiagonals upward: T(n,k) is the least integer m > k such that k^x * m^y = c^n for some positive integers c, x, and y where x < n and y < n; n >= 2, k >= 1. (OEIS A343881, NAME, revision 16; unpaginated.) All variables are natural numbers. Positivity of c, x and y and the strict bounds on both exponents are explicit.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (The source's proposed value).**
+
+$$\forall k \in \mathrm{Nat},\; A064549\left(k\right) = k \cdot \prod_{p \in \operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{primeFactors}\left(k\right)} p$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/Factorization/OeisA343881KageyPowerProducts.A064549` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* P. Kagey; OEIS Foundation Inc. (2021). *OEIS A343881, power-product minima and A064549*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A343881>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+a(n) = n * Product_{primes p|n} p. (OEIS A064549, NAME, revision 71; unpaginated.) The source index n is written k. Nat.primeFactors contains each prime divisor once.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (The eventual-equality conjecture).**
+
+$$claim \Leftrightarrow (\forall k \in \mathrm{Nat},\; (1 < k) \Rightarrow (\exists N \in \mathrm{Nat},\; \forall p \in \mathrm{Nat},\; (\operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{Prime}\left(p\right)) \Rightarrow ((N \le p) \Rightarrow ((\operatorname{if} h : (\exists m \in \mathrm{Nat},\; (k < m) \land (Works\left(p, k, m\right))) \operatorname{then} \operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{find}\left(h\right) \operatorname{else} 0) = A064549\left(k\right)))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/Factorization/OeisA343881KageyPowerProducts.claim` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* P. Kagey; OEIS Foundation Inc. (2021). *OEIS A343881, power-product minima and A064549*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A343881>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Table read by antidiagonals upward: T(n,k) is the least integer m > k such that k^x * m^y = c^n for some positive integers c, x, and y where x < n and y < n; n >= 2, k >= 1. (OEIS A343881, NAME, revision 16; unpaginated.) Conjecture: T(p,k) = A064549(k) for fixed k > 1 and sufficiently large p. (OEIS A343881, COMMENT, revision 16; unpaginated.) For every natural k greater than one there is a threshold N such that the equality holds for every prime p at least N. Nat.find selects the least larger factor; the value is zero when no such factor exists.
+
+**Theorem 1.4 (Refutation at k = 12).**
+
+$$\neg (\forall k \in \mathrm{Nat},\; (1 < k) \Rightarrow (\exists N \in \mathrm{Nat},\; \forall p \in \mathrm{Nat},\; (\operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{Prime}\left(p\right)) \Rightarrow ((N \le p) \Rightarrow ((\operatorname{if} h : (\exists m \in \mathrm{Nat},\; (k < m) \land (Works\left(p, k, m\right))) \operatorname{then} \operatorname{Nat}.\operatorname{find}\left(h\right) \operatorname{else} 0) = A064549\left(k\right)))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/Factorization/OeisA343881KageyPowerProducts.result` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Resolves.* `Problems/kagey343881-powerproducts` (refuted) by `D5/S3/Arith/Factorization/OeisA343881KageyPowerProducts.result`.
+
+<!-- scribe-open-problem-resolution-v1 {"problem_slug":"kagey343881-powerproducts","declaration_gid":"D5/S3/Arith/Factorization/OeisA343881KageyPowerProducts.result","resolution_kind":"refuted"} -->
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* P. Kagey; OEIS Foundation Inc. (2021). *OEIS A343881, power-product minima and A064549*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A343881>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+At k=12 the proposed value is 72. If 12^x times 72^y were an nth power, its prime coordinates would give n dividing both 2x+3y and x+2y. Twice the latter minus the former is y, so n divides y, contradicting 0<y<n. This obstruction holds for every natural n.
+
+For a prime p a larger factor exists: 27 works at p=2, while 144 works at p at least 3 with exponents p-2 and 1. Thus the least factor itself satisfies Works and cannot be 72. There are primes beyond every threshold, which disproves the eventual equality. The universal equality T(p,12)=144 for primes p at least 7 and a corrected formula for arbitrary k remain unproved here. The separate assertion that prime rows contain distinct integers also remains unresolved.
+

+import D5.S3.ConceptDynamics.InformationEscape.RegistrationTemplates
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+
+namespace D5.S3.Arith.Factorization.OeisA343881KageyPowerProducts
+
+open D5.S3.ConceptDynamics.InformationEscape.RegistrationTemplates (firstSuccess firstSuccess_eq_find)
+
+/-- `k^x * m^y = c^n` for some positive integers `c`, `x` and `y` where `x < n` and `y < n`. -/
+def Works (n k m : ℕ) : Prop :=
+  ∃ c x y : ℕ, 0 < c ∧ 0 < x ∧ 0 < y ∧ x < n ∧ y < n ∧ k ^ x * m ^ y = c ^ n
+
+/-- A064549: `a(n) = n * Product_{primes p|n} p`. -/
+def A064549 (k : ℕ) : ℕ := k * ∏ p ∈ k.primeFactors, p
+
+open Classical in
+/-- A343881 ("Conjecture: T(p,k) = A064549(k) for fixed k > 1 and sufficiently large p."), with `p`
+prime. -/
+def claim : Prop := ∀ k : ℕ, 1 < k → ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → N ≤ p →
+  (if h : ∃ m, k < m ∧ Works p k m then Nat.find h else 0) = A064549 k
+
+
+private theorem not_works_seventy_two (n : ℕ) : ¬ Works n 12 72 := by
+  rintro ⟨c, x, y, hc, hx, hy, hxn, hyn, hpow⟩
+  have f12 : (12 : ℕ).factorization = 2 • (2 : ℕ).factorization + (3 : ℕ).factorization := by
+    rw [show (12 : ℕ) = 2 ^ 2 * 3 by norm_num,
+      Nat.factorization_mul (by norm_num) (by norm_num), Nat.factorization_pow]
+  have f72 : (72 : ℕ).factorization = 3 • (2 : ℕ).factorization + 2 • (3 : ℕ).factorization := by
+    rw [show (72 : ℕ) = 2 ^ 3 * 3 ^ 2 by norm_num,
+      Nat.factorization_mul (by norm_num) (by norm_num), Nat.factorization_pow,
+      Nat.factorization_pow]
+  have hv (q : ℕ) : x * (12 : ℕ).factorization q + y * (72 : ℕ).factorization q =
+      n * c.factorization q := by
+    have h := congrArg (fun z : ℕ => z.factorization q) hpow
+    simpa only [Nat.factorization_mul (pow_ne_zero _ (by norm_num : (12 : ℕ) ≠ 0))
+      (pow_ne_zero _ (by norm_num : (72 : ℕ) ≠ 0)), Nat.factorization_pow,
+      Finsupp.add_apply, Finsupp.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul] using h
+  have h2 : 2 * x + 3 * y = n * c.factorization 2 := by
+    have h := hv 2
+    norm_num [f12, f72, Nat.prime_two.factorization, Nat.prime_three.factorization] at h
+    simp only [Nat.factorization_def _ Nat.prime_two] at h ⊢
+    omega
+  have h3 : x + 2 * y = n * c.factorization 3 := by
+    have h := hv 3
+    norm_num [f12, f72, Nat.prime_two.factorization, Nat.prime_three.factorization] at h
+    simp only [Nat.factorization_def _ Nat.prime_three] at h ⊢
+    omega
+  have d2 : n ∣ 2 * x + 3 * y := ⟨c.factorization 2, h2⟩
+  have d3 : n ∣ x + 2 * y := ⟨c.factorization 3, h3⟩
+  have dy : n ∣ y := by
+    have hd := Nat.dvd_sub (Nat.dvd_mul_left_of_dvd d3 2) d2
+    have he : 2 * (x + 2 * y) - (2 * x + 3 * y) = y := by omega
+    rwa [he] at hd
+  have hnle : n ≤ y := Nat.le_of_dvd hy dy
+  omega
+
+private theorem defined_at_twelve (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) : ∃ m, 12 < m ∧ Works p 12 m := by
+  by_cases hp2 : p = 2
+  · subst p
+    exact ⟨27, by norm_num, 18, 1, 1, by norm_num⟩
+  · have hp3 : 3 ≤ p := by have := hp.two_le; omega
+    refine ⟨144, by norm_num, 12, p - 2, 1, by norm_num, by omega,
+      by norm_num, by omega, by omega, ?_⟩
+    rw [pow_one, show (144 : ℕ) = 12 ^ 2 by norm_num, ← pow_add,
+      Nat.sub_add_cancel (by omega : 2 ≤ p)]
+
+theorem result : ¬ D5.S3.Arith.Factorization.OeisA343881KageyPowerProducts.claim := by
+  classical
+  intro hclaim
+  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := hclaim 12 (by norm_num)
+  obtain ⟨p, hNp, hp⟩ := Nat.exists_infinite_primes N
+  have ha : A064549 12 = 72 := by
+    have h : Nat.primeFactors 12 = {2, 3} := by
+      rw [show (12 : ℕ) = 2 ^ 2 * 3 by norm_num, Nat.primeFactors_mul (by norm_num) (by norm_num),
+        Nat.primeFactors_prime_pow (by norm_num) Nat.prime_two, Nat.prime_three.primeFactors]
+      rfl
+    simp [A064549, h]
+  let P : ℕ → Prop := fun m => 12 < m ∧ Works p 12 m
+  have he := defined_at_twelve p hp
+  have hmin : @Nat.find P (Classical.decPred P) he = Nat.find he := by
+    exact Nat.find.congr_simp rfl he
+  have ht : firstSuccess P = 72 := by
+    rw [firstSuccess_eq_find he, hmin]
+    have h := (hN p hp hNp).trans ha
+    rwa [dite_eq_left he] at h
+  have hw : Works p 12 (firstSuccess P) := by
+    rw [firstSuccess_eq_find he]
+    exact (@Nat.find_spec P (Classical.decPred P) he).2
+  exact not_works_seventy_two p (ht ▸ hw)
+
+end D5.S3.Arith.Factorization.OeisA343881KageyPowerProducts

+# Kagey's A343881 eventual equality conjecture
+
+## Problem
+
+P. Kagey's OEIS A343881 entry (revision 16) defines $T(n,k)$ as the least
+$m>k$ for which $k^x m^y=c^n$ with positive natural $c,x,y$ and $x,y<n$, and
+states:
+
+> Conjecture: T(p,k) = A064549(k) for fixed k > 1 and sufficiently large p.
+
+The entry defines $A064549(k)=k\prod_{q\mid k, q\ \mathrm{prime}}q$. Issue
+[#18686](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/issues/18686)
+preregistered the literal prime-threshold claim. The settling declaration
+is `D5/S3/Arith/Factorization/OeisA343881KageyPowerProducts.result : ¬ claim`.
+
+### Statement echo
+
+| Source clause | Lean counterpart | Fidelity |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| $k^x m^y=c^n$ with positive $c,x,y$ and $x,y<n$ | `Works` | The existential variables, positivity, strict bounds and equation are literal. |
+| $T(n,k)$ is the least $m>k$ satisfying `Works`, with zero if none exists | the minimum expression in `claim` | The `Nat.find`/zero convention is inlined literally in the claim. |
+| $A064549(k)=k\prod_{q\mid k}q$ | `A064549` | `Nat.primeFactors` gives the prime divisor product. |
+| eventual equality for every fixed $k>1$ and all sufficiently large prime $p$ | `claim` | The threshold, prime hypothesis and equality are retained. |
+| $T(p,12)=144$ for every prime $p\ge7$ | no delivered declaration | This stronger corrected statement remains open. |
+
+## Motivation
+
+At $k=12$, the source value is $A064549(12)=72$. The settling result shows
+that 72 cannot satisfy the source power-product condition for any natural
+exponent, while a valid larger factor exists at every prime exponent. Thus the
+proposed eventual equality fails at the first unequal-exponent neighbour of
+the source table.
+
+## Gap
+
+Issue #18686 records the source text, binding conventions, finite checker and
+bounded literature screen. The repository and searched external sources
+contained no settlement of this A343881 claim. Literature completeness is
+`ASSUMED-UNVERIFIED`; this bounded reading makes no worldwide absence or
+priority claim.
+
+## Route
+
+The proof compares prime-factorization coordinates of 12 and 72. If
+$12^x72^y=c^n$, the coordinates at 2 and 3 imply
+$n\mid 2x+3y$ and $n\mid x+2y$. Their determinant-one combination gives
+$n\mid y$, contradicting $0<y<n$. For a prime $p$, $m=27$ works at $p=2$,
+and $m=144$ works for $p\ge3$ with exponents $x=p-2$ and $y=1$. Infinitely
+many primes beyond every threshold then contradict the claimed equality at
+$k=12$.
+
+## Falsifier
+
+A natural $n$ and positive $x,y<n,c$ with $12^x72^y=c^n$ would invalidate
+the coordinate obstruction. Failure of the prime witness at $p=2$ or $p\ge3$
+would invalidate the existence step. A mismatch between the displayed claim
+and the OEIS convention would invalidate source fidelity.
+
+## Evidence
+
+The kernel-checked public declarations are `Works`, `A064549`, `claim` and
+`result`; private factorization and witness lemmas are consumed by `result`.
+The result's axiom closure is contained in
+{$\mathrm{propext}$, $\mathrm{Classical.choice}$, $\mathrm{Quot.sound}$}.
+The Scribe result carries `OpenProblemResolutionClaim` with slug
+`kagey343881-powerproducts` and `ResolutionKind.Refuted`.
+
+### Experiment
+
+The external checker is pinned to commit
+[8975668582f8222ff2b9e04de8b8e573eca4ed96](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing-experiments/tree/8975668582f8222ff2b9e04de8b8e573eca4ed96/docs/reports/oeis-a343881-kagey-power-products/),
+path `docs/reports/oeis-a343881-kagey-power-products/check.py`. Its SHA-256
+is `c05425172c41c9f6f524c4c6a5454a5e73a46f91806e2b022f29e232f79ec5ab`.
+The command is
+`python3 ../trureturing-experiments/docs/reports/oeis-a343881-kagey-power-products/check.py 100 43`.
+It checks the source table, the $k=12$ prime range, the absence of a working
+72 through $n=60$, and the proposed correction on $2\le k\le100$ at
+$p=31,37,41,43$. Its final output is `RESULT PASS` (exit code 0).
+
+## Triage
+
+### What the settlement shows
+
+| Item | Status and evidence kind | Evidence and boundary |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Mechanism: exponent vectors $v(12)=(2,1)$ and $v(72)=(3,2)$ force $n\mid y$, contradicting $0<y<n$. | Proved; kernel-checked | `not_works_seventy_two`; the argument is uniform in natural $n$. |
+| Extent: the obstruction holds for every natural $n$; a working $m$ exists at each prime exponent, so the large-prime conjecture is false. | Proved; kernel-checked | `not_works_seventy_two`, `defined_at_twelve` and `result`; the prime witness is 27 at $p=2$ and 144 for $p\ge3$. |
+| Numerical neighbour: $T(p,12)=144$ for primes $7\le p<48$, with values 27, 18, 54 at $p=2,3,5$. | Computed; pinned experiment | The checker command above; scope is exactly the listed finite prime range. |
+| Proposed correction on checked range: $T(p,k)=k^{1+1/g(k)}$ for $2\le k\le100$ and $p\in\{31,37,41,43\}$. | Computed; pinned experiment | The checker command above; this finite range does not establish a universal formula. |
+| Full corrected formula, including $T(p,12)=144$ for every prime $p\ge7$. | Open | No delivered declaration proves the universal minimum or threshold formula. |
+| Surviving neighbours: the equal-prime-exponent restriction and the distinct-integer prime-row assertion. | Open | Neither assertion is a premise or consequence of the delivered result. |
+
+The exact finite computation scope is the checker invocation above; any
+uniform extension beyond that scope remains open.
+
+## ASSUMED-UNVERIFIED
+
+Literature completeness is `ASSUMED-UNVERIFIED`. The OEIS source is
+unpaginated and its revision is a source reading, not a proof of publication
+priority. The finite checker supplies computed evidence only; the universal
+refutation is the kernel-checked `result`.
